title: Sonata For Improvisation
identity: Schott identifies Ludmila Ulehla's Sonata for Improvisation as a work for B-flat clarinet or soprano saxophone and piano. The original clarinet part was adapted to saxophone range, and both parts are included; tenor saxophone is also an option. LSU hosts John Perrine's 2002 DMA paper, which analyzes Ulehla's sonata alongside Phil Woods and Bill Dobbins works as repertoire combining jazz improvisation with formal models. Its public paper page is readable, but the linked PDF returned 403 in this pass.

evidence.claim: Publisher lists instrumentation, clarinet origin, included adapted sax part, optional tenor, free improvisation, and difficulty descriptor.

LSU Major Paper abstract identifies the Sonata for Improvisation as one of three crossover sonatas and says the works combine jazz improvisation with historical formal models; it is a Doctor of Musical Arts paper from 2002.
